tag: Episode 32 Side Story · Returning the Swallowed Songs
title: Returning the Swallowed Songs

beats.t: The fourth bell rang. Another line of Wu Qu's light went dark. Eight tolls remained until the twelfth.
You know I can't sing.
I know. You can't rap either.
Why bring that up now?!
Because everyone here already knows what you're bad at. That's why it's okay.
The fifth bell rang. Neo dropped to one knee and braced a hand on the floor. The gray had reached beneath his chin.
Hurry. I can't promise the rhythm, but I can add a low note.
I know twelve compatibility songs. All their lyrics are weird.
...What are you doing? Stop. It's ridiculous.
(It is. That's the idea. This time, the laughter won't be aimed at you.)
Yeoni cleared their throat. Even at karaoke, they were always on tambourine duty. But today there was no tambourine. Only their voice.
Ridiculous is fine. This time we'll be the ridiculous ones. You just listen.
Moka drew a breath. His tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
Then came the first line. Moka's voice cracked. Like a rooster crowing. Very loudly.
Yeoni burst out laughing. But they sang along through their laughter. They didn't know the words, so they followed the tune. They got that wrong too.
Ha ha. You're both a semitone flat.
Yundal joined in, laughing. He added strange lyrics: if the Four Pillars matched, everything matched; if they didn't, it was half price.
Neo sustained a low note. The Metal energy in his voice resonated through the iron walls. He was half a beat late.
It was a mess. They sounded like four people singing four different songs. But the tail's rhythm never faltered. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
Everyone's laughing. While they're singing.
(Yes. We're laughing now. Without laughing at anyone.)
Something spilled from Museong's eyes. He almost closed them, as he had onstage. Then he didn't. He watched the smiling faces until the end.
The sixth bell drowned in the song. No one heard it.
The song ended. Or rather, everyone stopped because they were out of breath. Moka leaned on his knees, panting.
Yeoni clapped. Moka and Yundal followed. Neo brought his trembling palms together too. His slightly delayed claps found their way into the rhythm.
The applause passed beyond the stage and gathered beneath it. The kneeling boy lifted his head toward the sound.
This is for that day. Late, huh? Years late. Sorry.
...But I didn't sing.
You did. You sang every last line that day. With your cracked voice. This applause is for the person who sang to the end.
The black feather in Museong's chest trembled. Its color changed from the tip downward: ink black to gray, gray to warm gold.
Prosperity Transformation. It really worked. Obstruction has turned to Prosperity.
The black threads stretching from the feather turned gold too. They no longer constricted Wu Qu. Instead, they poured light into the star.
The bound star breathed. Iron gray turned silver again. Black rust peeled from the walls like scales.
“...Thank you. What was blocked now flows. Metal was always a vessel for what flows.”
The gray receded from Neo's neck, past his shoulder and elbow, below his wrist. Only a coin-sized black stain remained on his fingertips.
I'll carry what's left. It isn't a debt to pass on to Wu Qu.
There you go again. You're telling me everything later.
I promised.
The gray lanterns piled in the corner lit one by one. Their light streamed through the door to their rightful owners.
The seventh bell rang. But the sound had changed. It spread clear and bright instead of clanging against metal. This bell wasn't counting down to noon. It announced an open door.
(Noon never came. The time Black Moon dragged forward has come loose.)
Yeoni crouched beside Neo and touched the remaining black stain. It was cold, like a piece of metal.
Earlier. When I spoke. Did it really not hurt?
It didn't. Your fire takes a different shape when you speak than when you shout.
(The shape of fire. Fire that explodes, and fire you light.)
Today, you lit it. So everyone sang beside that fire.
...Say things like that when your hand has healed.
Neo patted Yeoni's shoulder lightly. Once again, he was half a beat late.
In the corridor back to the market, Yundal slowed down. He held his gloved right hand against his chest.
Yundal. Your hand.
I swallowed rather a lot of thread earlier. The hole has spread past my wrist.
A black crack crept above his wrist from the edge of the glove, like a fine line of ink.
I'm fine. With Wu Qu freed, your chart should be clearer too, my lady. I've protected my business capital.
There it is again. Nobody's allowed to say they're fine anymore. From now on, saying it costs a fine.
How much?
Ten skewers. Pay Moka.
The market's star lamps glowed again. Color returned to the gray cheeks of the star people. Someone hummed while bargaining.
A little star child came running from the end of the corridor. At the sight of Museong, the child hesitated, then offered a palm-sized lantern. The very lantern confiscated at the judgment stand.
For me? But I'm the one who took it.
Instead of answering, the child pressed the lantern into Museong's hand and ran off. A few steps later, the child turned and stuck out a tongue.
Was that forgiveness or teasing?
Both. That's how we do it on the island.
Ever since the feather turned gold, my wings won't grow. I'm just a person.
Come to the island. They're bringing back the sunrise stage this year. I'll squeeze you in beside my grill.
What if my voice cracks again?
Then we'll laugh again. And clap again. That's what a stage is.
Museong laughed. His voice was hoarse, but it was unmistakably laughter.
There's one thing I should tell you. The voice that gave me the feather used to say something a lot. That there's a vessel in the Wealth room.
A vessel.
The Xu room. No star person who went in ever came back. And I heard chains dragging in there. Every time it rained.
(Chains. Rain. ...Seo Hanbi.)
